summary_paragraph: A male patient with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, history of bladder cancer with ileal conduit, and recent UTI treated for multidrug-resistant organisms was admitted for bright red blood per rectum, abdominal pain, and weakness. His hemoglobin was stable at 7.3 g/dL and dropped slightly to 7.1 g/dL, and he received one unit of packed red blood cells. CT abdomen and pelvis showed no acute pathology but confirmed patent TIPS and cirrhosis. Urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, prompting treatment with cefepime. Abdominal pain was managed with a switch from oxycodone to Dilaudid. The patient declined further interventions and left against medical advice after two days, with understanding of the risks and instructions to continue antibiotics and follow up with specialists.
